correctness.rationale: Explicit Brownian regeneration at Poisson reset times gives an exponential-age symmetric-Laplace integer jump transform. The analytically dominant renewal pole yields long-time cumulant derivatives of an implicit hyperbolic equation. Coefficient extraction is checked by two algebraic forms, with the sixth coefficient equal to a strictly positive factor times N(a). Taylor coefficients are exactly signed: n=4 positive, n=5..11 negative, n>=12 positive by three strict exponential-domination inequalities. Dividing N(sqrt z) by z^4 and differentiating shows a unique minimum; an exact rational enclosure for e proves N(1)<0 and exponential asymptotics yield N(a)>0 eventually. Thus exactly two simple positive zeros. CHECK.py independently runs 30 exact/symbolic/numerical tests. Mathematical limitations and the role of local analytic renewal asymptotics are stated in RESULT.md.

originality.rationale: The exact two-transition sixth-cumulant sign classification is not stated by the motivating 2024 article, the closely related general analytic SCGF result, or the prior fourth-cumulant theorem. The full counting-field equation and formal sixth-order differentiation are explicitly treated as prior/implied work, not claimed as new; originality is in the rigorous exactly-two-positive-zeros classification of the sixth coefficient, which needs an infinite coefficient-sign and rational boundary argument. Direct published full-text comparisons and six semantic database queries found no covering statement; residual unindexed literature risk remains.
residual_risks: A generic renewal or Markov-additive counting-field theorem could imply the sixth-cumulant sign result after a nontrivial specialization not recognized here.
Some supplemental material accompanying the motivating 2024 article was not independently inspected; its treatment of fluctuations beyond diffusion is uncertain.

value.rationale: The sixth cumulant is a physically meaningful first unclassified higher-order transport statistic beyond known diffusivity and the universally positive fourth cumulant. Its exactly two sign transitions distinguish three fluctuation regimes that no lower-order positivity statement determines. A complete global parameter classification and rigorous root-count theorem are structurally motivated, not an arbitrary numerical slice; no broad conjecture or unrelated incremental computation is substituted.
